draft.title: Tectonic forces and landforms
card: The Earth's outer layer is broken into large slabs of rock called tectonic plates. They move very slowly, only a few centimetres a year. Where they meet or pull apart, they shape the land.
Folding
when plates push together, layers of rock can bend into folds. Over millions of years this can build fold mountains, such as the Himalayas.
Faulting
when rock cracks and blocks of land move along the crack, this is a fault. If plates pull apart, a block of land can drop between two faults to form a rift valley, such as the East African Rift.
Volcano
a landform built where magma (melted rock) reaches the surface. The magma erupts as lava and ash, which pile up around the opening.
draft.remember: Plates push, pull and crack the land into mountains, rift valleys and volcanoes.

a.q: Two tectonic plates push together and layers of rock bend into folds over millions of years. Which landform can this build?
a.why: Plates pushing together bend rock into folds, and over a very long time this can build fold mountains. A rift valley is the tempting wrong answer, but it forms where plates pull apart and a block of land drops.
a.clue: Think about what happens to rock layers when they are squeezed.

b.q: Two plates under a region are slowly pulling apart. A long block of land drops between two faults. What landform is forming?
b.why: Plates pulling apart can crack the rock into faults, and a block of land between them can drop to make a rift valley. Fold mountains are tempting, but they come from plates pushing together and bending rock, not from a block dropping.
b.clue: Look at the direction the plates are moving and at what the land block does.

a.q: Two plates push together. Over millions of years, the squeezing crumples flat layers of rock and pushes them upwards. Which landform is built from this crumpled rock?
a.why: When plates push together, rock layers can bend, and over a very long time the bent layers can build fold mountains. A volcano is tempting, but it is built from lava and ash piling up where magma reaches the surface, not from squeezed rock layers.
a.clue: What happens to rock layers when they are squeezed from both sides?
